preamble: Retroflexion of the palato-alveolar affricate [tʃ] to the retroflex [ʈʂ] occurred in the Mamean branch of Mayan as part of a chain shift (*r > t, *t > tʃ, *tʃ > ʈʂ), and in Polish, where Proto-Slavic *č [tʃ] became the retroflex (flat postalveolar) cz [ʈʂ] that contrasts with alveolo-palatal ć [tɕ].

examples.note: Mamean (Mam, Tektitek, Awakatek, Ixil) shifted *tʃ to the retroflex affricate tx as one step of a chain shift (*r > t, *t > tʃ, *tʃ > ʈʂ); Q'anjob'alan languages such as Akatek ak'atx share the retroflex.

sources: Bennett, R. (2016). Mayan phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10(10): 469–514. https://doi.org/10.1111/lnc3.12148
